products.title: Products (RHP)
products.body:
- Used in water treatment as a dechlorinating agent, in manufacture of caramel colour as a reducing agent and in pulp/bamboo pulp and paper industry as a bleaching agent. Manufactured at Manufacturing Unit - I (Vatva). Available in food grade and technical grade.
- Used as a preservative in food and beverages, oxygen scavenger in oil drilling and effluent treatment, cyanide removal in gold mining, reducing agent in dyes/dye intermediates and textile dyeing, dechlorinating agent in water treatment and bleaching agent in acrylic fibre manufacture. Manufactured at Manufacturing Unit - I (Vatva). The FY24 revenue table also carries an 'S.B.S. liquor' line.
- Described as a higher-grade derivative of sodium bisulphite. Used as a food preservative in sea food processing and biscuits, in shrimp farming, as an oxygen scavenger in oil drilling, for cyanide removal in gold refining, as a dechlorinating agent in water treatment and as a bleaching agent in acrylic fibre manufacture. Manufactured at Manufacturing Unit - I (Vatva).
- Used as a preservative and antioxidant in food and beverages, reducing agent in detoxification of chromic acid in electroplating, chemical intermediate in sulfosuccinates for detergents, reducing agent in disperse dyes and surfactants, oxygen scavenger in boiler feed water treatment and bleaching agent in pulp and paper. Manufactured at Manufacturing Unit - II Phase I (Bavla), commercial production w.e.f. February 2025.
- These lines appear in the DRHP's product-wise revenue table and correspond to the 'Trading' component of revenue from operations (Trading was Rs 714.62 lakhs / 10.13% of the FY26 split table total and Rs 51.51 lakhs in FY24; nil in FY25 and in the two months ended May 31, 2026). The DRHP does not separately state which of these lines are traded versus manufactured beyond the manufacturing/trading split.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: The Red Herring Prospectus does not describe any backward- or forward-integration programme for the Company itself. Its primary raw materials - sulphur dioxide, sodium hydroxide and sodium carbonate (with anhydrous ammonia, soda ash light, caustic soda flakes and caustic lye also material) - are bought from a diversified third-party supplier base located in India, and the Company states it has not entered into any long-term supply arrangement or agreement with its suppliers. The DRHP frames its sourcing advantage as locational rather than integrated: the manufacturing units are described as strategically located in close proximity to industries that generate liquified sulphur dioxide, which the Company says gives consistent and reliable sources of key raw materials and reduces logistics cost and lead time. The Company moved in the opposite direction on upstream processing in Fiscal 2019, when it transitioned from using sulphur burning furnaces to procuring liquefied sulphur dioxide (SO2), which it states improved production efficiency, reduced emissions and enhanced environmental compliance. For Phase II of Manufacturing Unit - II the Company proposes to install a sulphur burner system with a waste heat boiler that will generate fuel-free steam for plant operations without relying on external fuel sources - an in-house utility rather than product capacity. Downstream, the Company sells business-to-business directly through its own India-based sales and marketing team and states that it currently does not have any sales and distribution network for its domestic and export customers; it intends to build a distribution network in Europe, North America and South America. It has not entered into any technical or other collaboration or joint venture agreement, and it uses third-party logistics for both inbound raw materials and outbound finished goods, with no long-term contracts with any logistics service provider. Trading of bought-out goods (soda ash dense, Ecosoft, high carbon ferro chrome and similar lines) sits alongside manufacturing in revenue from operations.

demand_drivers.title: Seasonality (RHP report)
demand_drivers.body: Under 'Seasonality of Business' in Management's Discussion and Analysis, the Red Herring Prospectus states: 'Except as mentioned in this chapter, our business is not subject to seasonal variations.' No quantified seasonality pattern is disclosed elsewhere in the business or risk-factor text.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Our business operations are primarily engaged in the manufacture and supply of sulphur-based inorganic chemicals, which have critical applications in the food and beverages, oil drilling and chemical industries.
- The chemical industry, being diverse and competitive, is subject to volatility in raw material prices, energy costs, technological shifts, and global trade
- We have not faced any such instances in the past, however, any adverse developments in one or more of these sectors, such as a downturn in demand, regulatory tightening, commodity price fluctuations, or increased competition, may lead to a decline in demand for our products.
- Moreover, customers may shift to lower-priced alternatives or substitutes, which could adversely affect our pricing, margins, and overall financial performance.
- Our Company derives revenue from diversified customers.
- Our inability to acquire new customers or loss of all or a substantial portion of any of our major customers, for any reason and/or continued reduction of the business from them, could have a material adverse impact on our business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.
- Our Company derives revenues from diversified customers.
- We cannot assure that we will be able to maintain historic levels of business from our top one (1), five (5) and ten (10) customers, or that we will be able to reduce customer concentration in the future.
